<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. VIII.|ACCORDING TO S. MATTHEW.|19}}</noinclude>doctrine. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=29}}† For he vvas teaching them as hauing povver, and not as their Scribes and Pharisees.

{{c|{{larger|A N N O T A T I O N S}}}}
{{c|{{sc|Chap. VII.}}}}

''1. Iudge not.''] It is no Christian part to iudge il of mens actes which be in them selues good and may procede of good meaning, or of mans inward meanings and intentions which we can not see: of which fault they must beware that are to suspicious and giuen to deeme alwayes the worst of other men. But to say, that Iudas, or an Heretike euidently knowen to die obstinatly in heresie, is damned, and in al other playne and manifest cases to iudge, is not forbidden.

''6. Holy to dogges.''] {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Worthy receiuing.}}No holy Sacrament and specially that of our Sauiours blessed body, must be geuen wittingly to the vnworthy, that is, to them that haue not by confession of al mortal sinnes examined and proued them selues. See the Annot. ''1. Cor.11, 27. 28, 29''.

''8. Euery one that asketh.''] Al things that we aske necessarie to saluation with humilitie, attention, continuance, and other dewe circumstances, God wil vndoubtedly graunt when it is best for vs.

''15. Clothing of sheepe.''] {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Heretikes wolues in sheepe-skinnes.}}Extraordinarie apparance of zeale and holines is the sheepes cote in some Heretikes: but these of this time weare not that garment much, being men of vnsatiable sinne. This is rather their garment, common to them with al other Heretikes, to crake much of the word of the Lord, and by pretensed allegations and {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Ro. 16, 18.''}}sweete wordes of benediction, and specially by promise of knowledge, light and libertie of the Gospel, to seduce the simple and the sinful.

''16. Fruites.''] {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Heretikes knowen by their fruites.}}These are the fruites which Heretikes are knowen by, diuision from the whole Churche, diuision among them selues, taking to them selues new names and new maisters, inconstancie in doctrine, disobedience both to others and namely to spiritual officers, loue and liking of them selues, pride and intolerable vaunting of their owne knowledge aboue al the holy Doctors, corruption, falsification, and quite denying of the parts of Scriptures that specially make agaynst them, and these be common to al Heretikes lightly. Othersome are more peculiar to these of our time, as Incestuous Mariages of vowed persons, Spoile of Churches, Sacrilege and profanation of al holy things, and many other special poynts of doctrine, directly tending to the corruption of good life in al states.

''21. Lord, Lord.''] These men haue faith, otherwise they could not inuocate, ''Lord, Lord: Ro. 10.'' But here we see that to beleeue is not ynough, and that not only infidelitie is sinne, as Luther teacheth. {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Not only faith.}}Yea Catholikes also that worke true miracles in the name of our Lord, and by neuer so great fayth, yet without the workes of iustice shal not be saued. ''1. Cor. 13.'' Agayne, consider here, who they are that haue so often in their mouth, ''The Lord, the Lord,'' and how litle it shal auaile them, that set so litle ''Esa. 53, 4. 1. Pet. 2, 24.''

''Lu.9, 57.''

{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. VIII.}}}}}}

{{c|''Immediatly after his Sermon (to confirme his doctrine with a miracle) he cureth a Leper. 5. But aboue him and al other Iewes, he commendeth the faith of the Centurion, who was a Gentil: and foretelleth by that occasion, the vocation of the Gentiles, and reprobation of the Iewes. 14. In Peters house he sheweth great grace. 18. In the way to the sea he speaketh with two, of folowing him: 23. and vpon the sea commaundeth the tempest: 28. and beyond the sea he manifesteth the deuils malice agaynst man, in an heard of swine.''}} {{dropinitial|A|fl={{verse|chapter=8|verse=1}}}}ND {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel on the 3. Sunday after the Epiphanie.}}when he was come downe from the mountaine, great multitudes folowed him: {{verse|chapter=8|verse=2}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mr. 1, 40. Lu. 5, 12.''}}* behold a leper came and adored him saying, Lord, if thou wilt, thou canst make me cleane. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=3}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} stretching forth his hand, touched him, saying. I wil. be thou made cleane. And forthwith, his leprosy was made cleane. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=4}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} sayth to<noinclude>{{rh||C ij|him,}}</noinclude>
